# Introduction

Often, a protein of interest is only known by its sequence, e.g. because it
comes from a newly sequenced genome. `OmaDB` provides two functions for
such sequences: `mapSequence()` identifies the proteins in the OMA Browser
that match a sequence exactly or approximately, and `annotateSequence()`
predicts Gene Ontology annotations for a sequence based on the
annotations of the closest proteins in OMA (OMA FastMap). See the vignette
"Get started with OmaDB" for an introduction to the package.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("OmaDB")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(OmaDB)
```

# Mapping a sequence

The query can be a character string or an `AAString` object of the
`r Biocpkg("Biostrings")` package:

```{r sequence}
sequence <- Biostrings::AAString(paste0(
    "MNDPSLLGYPNVGPQQQQQQQQQQHAGLLGKGTPNALQQQLHMNQLTGIPPPGLMNNSDVHTSSNNNS",
    "RQLLDQLANGNANMLNMNMDNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGGGSGVMMNASTAAVNSIGMVPTVGTPVNINVN",
    "ASNPLLHPHLDDPSLLNNPIWKLQLHLAAVSAQSLGQPNIYARQNAMKKYLATQQAQQAQQQAQQQAQ",
    "QQVPGPFGPGPQAAPPALQPTDFQQSHIAEASKSLVDCTKQALMEMADTLTDSKTAKKQQPTGDSTPS",
    "GTATNSAVSTPLTPKIELFANGKDEANQALLQHKKLSQYSIDEDDDIENRMVMPKDSKYDDQLWHALD",
    "LSNLQIFNISANIFKYDFLTRLYLNGNSLTELPAEIKNLSNLRVLDLSHNRLTSLPAELGSCFQLKYF",
    "YFFDNMVTTLPWEFGNLCNLQFLGVEGNPLEKQFLKILTEKSVTGLIFYLRDNRPEIPLPHER"))
sequence
```

```{r map}
res <- mapSequence(sequence)
res$identified_by
res$targets[, c("omaid", "canonicalid", "species.species")]
```

The search strategy can be set to `"exact"`, `"approximate"` or `"mixed"`
(the default: approximate search is only used if no exact match is
found). The matching protein can then be explored further, e.g. its
orthologs:

```{r orthologs}
target <- getProtein(res$targets$omaid[1])
head(target$orthologs[, c("omaid", "species.species", "rel_type")])
```

# Function prediction

`annotateSequence()` predicts Gene Ontology annotations of a sequence,
which does not need to be in the OMA Browser. The predictions are returned
in the columns of the GAF format; the column `With` indicates the protein
the annotation is derived from.

```{r annotate}
go <- annotateSequence(sequence)
nrow(go)
head(go[, c("GO_ID", "GO_name", "Aspect", "With")])
```
